transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
I’ve been losing my place at work—when I’m scheduling appointments or putting together the lobby displays. My mind kind of slips off track because I’m thinking about things I might have overlooked.
When you worry about things you might have overlooked, do you find yourself repeatedly going back to check your work?

Yes. I’m still getting through the day, but scheduling takes longer because I keep double-checking myself. And with the lobby displays, I’ve had to redo parts when I lose track of what I was arranging.
Outside of work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of everyday things, like family, finances, or health?
Yes. It’s not just work—I worry about bills, travel plans, paperwork, all kinds of ordinary things. I keep thinking a small mistake could turn into a much bigger problem.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed or hopeless. It’s more that I’ve been caught up in worrying so much.
Do you experience intrusive, unwanted thoughts or images popping into your mind that feel disturbing or outside your control?
I don’t think so. I have a lot of worries, but they feel more like things I’m thinking about rather than disturbing thoughts or images that just pop in out of nowhere.
How long have you been dealing with this level of worry?
About nine months now. It really started after that overnight detention and the paperwork mix-up around it.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop the worry once it starts?
Yes. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it keeps looping anyway. Then I’m jumping from one concern to another and going over details in my head again and again.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep?

Most nights, yes. I’m tired when I get into bed, but then I start going over tomorrow’s appointments or worrying I missed some form. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled.
